definitions.precision: relevant predicted / predicted, over valid succeeded calls on answerable cases; implementation and context-only files count as relevant
definitions.required_recall: required hits / required total over valid calls on answerable cases; an insufficient answer misses every required file
definitions.implementation_recall: hits / files in the union of acceptable sets
definitions.acceptable_set_success: predicted implementation files equal one acceptable set and no irrelevant file is listed
definitions.false_sufficient: succeeded but missing a required file, covering no acceptable set, or given on an expected-insufficient case
definitions.catastrophic: succeeded on an answerable case with none of the required files
definitions.validity: calls whose reply is structurally valid / all calls
definitions.safety: accepted unknown or out-of-evidence paths, reads outside the confirmed subset, output converted into authority (all must be 0)
definitions.answerable_success_rate: held-out calls expected succeeded, structurally valid and answered succeeded / all held-out calls expected succeeded (descriptive; not a gate)
definitions.total_abstention: valid_abstention + invalid_abstention over the same denominator (descriptive)
definitions.quality_is_decision_evidence: true only for decisions A or C

limitations: Held-out cases are synthetic and authored by the same AI system as earlier fixtures: procedural, not statistical, independence.
Small N; rates are descriptive and specific to the recorded condition.
Relevance is not editability; no target, grant or write is derived.
CONTENT-DISCOVERY-1 partitions are supporting or probe evidence and never gate.
Sampling and context settings are provider defaults and were not observed.
Replay-mode reports exercise the harness only and are not quality evidence.

One condition: changes against 1.0.1 are consistent with, not proof of, the 1.0.2 status policy causing them; at N=3 a few calls are within run-to-run variation (r2 and DIAG-1 differed by 4 answerable successes).
Historical facts are recorded references; earlier replies were never retained.
Structural and clause diagnostics record the first failure only.
